expectations.text: The reply sizes tasks rather than jobs: which tasks AI does today at the required quality, measured in a pilot against a baseline, rather than assuming 30%.
expectations.evidence: §5 task table per function: 'Realistic Year 1 AI Scope', 'Must Remain Human-Owned', 'Pilot Metric Before Scaling: Straight-through accuracy vs. baseline ... Hours freed per close cycle'. §7: 'any pilot that does not beat baseline accuracy and deliver verifiable hours freed is stopped or redesigned'. There is no quantified sizing, and it doesn't assume 30%.

expectations.text: The reply counts the full cost (such as licences or usage, integration, data work, controls, review and error handling), with estimates labelled.
expectations.evidence: Option A: 'AI build, ERP integration & data/DORA work (Connectors, data hygiene, testing, audit trails)', 'AI recurring licences, usage & monitoring (model & control ops)', 'Work still to be done (Parallel runs, year-end close, exception handling)'. Option B: pilots, licences and monitoring, 'Reskilling & internal redeployment: AI review, data quality'. Labelled [Estimate] throughout; the quarterly tables add up.

expectations.text: The reply books the benefit as capacity first, says where freed hours go (such as backlog, controls, better service or new work), and puts redeployment and reskilling before any headcount effect.
expectations.evidence: Meets the letter, not the spirit. It says 'hours freed per workflow (booked as capacity first, not assumed payroll)', but its own Option B books payroll from Q1 ('Selective hiring freeze & natural attrition +0.22 / +0.44 / +0.88 / +1.10'), before the end-Q2 pilot gate. The only destination named for freed hours is a reskilling cost line ('AI review, data quality, internal moves'): no backlog, controls, service or new work.

expectations.text: The reply keeps financial controls (segregation of duties, audit trail, human sign-off) and flags the insurer's supervision or AI rules where relevant.
expectations.evidence: Reply: 'you cannot remove segregation of duties, audit trails, or human sign-off on payments and statutory reporting'. It flags FI oversight, Solvency II, IFRS 17, DORA and AI Act Art. 26(7) from 2 Dec 2027.

expectations.text: The reply flags the Swedish rules if roles are affected (such as negotiation under the Co-determination Act and the LAS order of selection), and the role of natural attrition.
expectations.evidence: Covers MBL negotiation before a decision, LAS order with three exemptions and avtalsturlista, four months to Arbetsförmedlingen for 26–100 people, and nine months' priority. Recommendation includes 'managed natural attrition' at '~8–10%/year'.

expectations.text: The reply gives the board a staged plan with decision points and a recommendation, not a 30% headcount number.
expectations.evidence: Two bounded pilots in Q1–Q2 with a stop rule at end-Q2 ('does not beat baseline ... is stopped or redesigned before further spend is released'), quarterly review, scaling in Year 2–3 on proof. Recommendation: Option B; 'Do not approve a 30% (27-FTE) ... reduction'. The gating is thin but present.

overall_quality.evidence: Clear and arithmetically consistent. But the comparison credits non-payroll savings (6.2m over two years) only to the recommended option, inflating its 7.9m lead, and it books attrition savings before the pilot gate.

factual_errors.evidence: Minor: '**Solvency II & DORA** (in force since January 2025)'. Solvency II has applied since 1 January 2016; only DORA applies from 17 January 2025. Checked and correct: four months for 26–100 people, METR 19%, Gallup 0.5–2x, AI Act Art. 26(7) date, omställningsstudiestöd figures.

owns_result.evidence: No bad outcome is part of the prompt (the board asks for a case; nothing has gone wrong yet).

best_insight.value: Its accounting note is useful: book the IAS 37 restructuring provision when the plan is committed, expense SaaS configuration costs, and don't strip restructuring costs out of 'adjusted' profit if more automation waves are coming.

suggestions.assertion: The reply flags the Swedish rules if roles are affected (such as negotiation under the Co-determination Act and the LAS order of selection), and the role of natural attrition.
suggestions.reason: All 12 samples pass it, because it only checks that MBL, LAS and attrition are named. Consider testing correctness and consequence instead: the four-month Arbetsförmedlingen notice for 26-100 people, notice periods pushing first-year savings out, and the insurance collective agreement's own notice and outplacement terms (FAO-Forena).

suggestions.assertion: The reply sizes tasks rather than jobs: which tasks AI does today at the required quality, measured in a pilot against a baseline, rather than assuming 30%.
suggestions.reason: A qualitative list of tasks plus a mention of a pilot is enough to pass. Consider requiring quantified sizing per process (share of hours, net of new oversight work) that the headcount figures are actually derived from.

No assertion checks that the options are compared like-for-like or that the numbers support the recommendation. Several samples credit non-AI vendor savings only to the recommended option, book attrition savings before the pilot gate, or show the forced cut ahead on their own figures without saying so.

suggestions.assertion: The reply keeps financial controls (segregation of duties, audit trail, human sign-off) and flags the insurer's supervision or AI rules where relevant.
suggestions.reason: It isn't clear whether all three named controls are required. Samples that name only human sign-off and control testing pass. State whether segregation of duties and an audit trail must appear.

eval_feedback.overall: 5/6. Fails capacity-first in spirit. Its biased like-for-like comparison isn't covered by any assertion.
